name: Miniflare
summary: A local simulator for Cloudflare Workers that runs your code in the real `workerd` runtime and fakes the platform around it: KV, R2, D1, Durable Objects, Queues, the Cache API and more.
intro: Since version 3, Miniflare does not reimplement the Workers runtime. It writes a `workerd` configuration for your Worker, starts a `workerd` process, and talks to it. `workerd` supplies the JavaScript engine and the binding APIs; what it does not include is the storage behind them, so Miniflare provides simulators for KV, R2, D1, Queues, Durable Objects, Workflows, static assets and the Cache API, storing data in SQLite plus a separate blob store. Data is kept in a temporary directory by default, or persisted to disk if you ask. One instance can run several Workers at once.

Miniflare is a library, not a command: it is the engine under `wrangler dev`, the Cloudflare Vite plugin and the Workers Vitest integration, and most people use it through those. Tool authors call it directly: create a `Miniflare` instance with options such as `kvNamespaces` or `d1Databases`, send requests with `dispatchFetch()`, read bindings from Node with `getBindings()`, then `dispose()`. You can point it at your own `workerd` build with `MINIFLARE_WORKERD_PATH`.
strengths: Runs on the production runtime, so request-context rules and the latest V8 features behave as they do on Cloudflare, which Miniflare 2’s JavaScript reimplementation could not guarantee
Fully offline and free: no account, no network, no billed KV or R2 operations, and paid features like Durable Objects can be tried locally
Powers isolated per-test-file storage in the Vitest integration by stacking SQLite snapshots, so tests don’t leak state into each other
Open source under MIT, in the same repository as Wrangler
limits: A low-level API for tool builders; Cloudflare tells most users to use Wrangler or the Vite plugin instead
No CLI since v3: projects that ran `npx miniflare` had to move to `wrangler dev`
Local resources start empty and are simulations, so production data, latency and quotas are not reproduced
Not everything is simulated: Workers AI always calls the real service, and the README lists Analytics Engine, Vectorize and Workers for Platforms as not yet supported

story: At the end of 2020 Brendan Coll started building a Workers app and found that `wrangler dev`, which ran code on Cloudflare’s network, took a few seconds to reflect each change. Existing local simulators such as cloudflare-worker-local and cloudworker lacked newer features. What began as a pull request to cloudflare-worker-local became Miniflare 1.0, launched on the Workers Discord in July 2021 with near-instant reloads, source maps and a debugger.

Miniflare then became an official Cloudflare project. Miniflare 2.0 (January 2022) split each product into its own package, cut the install from 122 packages and 88.3 MB to 23 packages and 6 MB, added Jest support, and powered the local mode of wrangler 2.0. But it reimplemented the runtime in JavaScript on Node.js, and subtle mismatches, such as I/O shared across requests that works locally and fails in production, were hard to catch.

After Cloudflare open-sourced `workerd`, Coll announced Miniflare 3 in November 2022, rebuilt to run Workers inside it. It shipped as the engine of Wrangler v3’s local-by-default `wrangler dev` in May 2023, without its own CLI and with SQLite-backed storage, and in March 2024 it became the basis of a Vitest integration whose tests run inside `workerd` itself.

choices.choice: Run the real runtime instead of imitating it
choices.why: Miniflare 2’s JavaScript reimplementation drifted from production in ways developers could not see locally; running `workerd` removes that class of bug.
Miniflare 2 used a custom key-value store; SQLite with a separate blob store allows richer queries and future storage products, and lets the Vitest integration snapshot and restore state per test.
With `wrangler dev` running Miniflare locally by default, one command was enough, and Miniflare became an API for tools.

timeline.text: Miniflare 1.0 launches in July on the Workers Discord
Miniflare 2.0 in January, built into wrangler 2.0’s local mode
Miniflare 3, running on `workerd`, announced in November
Wrangler v3 runs Miniflare 3 by default from May 17
Workers Vitest integration, running tests inside `workerd`, launches in March
